ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AB\parallel CD\parallel EF$, if $AC=6, CE=3, DF=2$, then what is the length of $BD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because AB\parallel CD\parallel EF$,\\
$\therefore \frac{AC}{CE}=\frac{BD}{DF}$,\\
$\because AC=6, CE=3, DF=2$,\\
$\therefore \frac{6}{3}=\frac{BD}{2}$,\\
Solving this, we get: $BD=\boxed{4}$.

method.method_draft: Use similar triangles after extending the two transversals. From the image, extend the left transversal through A,C,E and the right transversal through B,D,F until they meet at a point P. Because AB, CD, and EF are parallel, triangles PAB, PCD, and PEF are similar. Similarity implies that the differences between corresponding distances along the two transversals are proportional, so the segment between the top and middle parallels on the left corresponds to the segment between the top and middle parallels on the right, and the segment between the middle and bottom parallels on the left corresponds to the segment between the middle and bottom parallels on the right. Thus AC/CE = BD/DF. Using the text values, 6/3 = BD/2, giving BD=4.
